Hi Ana — thanks for the clear profile. Attached is a concise options sheet with three reservation paths and fallback guidance (attached: LumenRx_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf). TL;DR summary below.

Option A — Anchor (cost-efficient, longer lead):
- Cluster: Reserved pool of 8x A100-80GB equiv GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed floor: 8 GPUs (steady-state)
- Ramp: 2-week warm-up (traffic shaping) then full traffic at week 4; option to scale +8 GPUs after month 3 if throughput growth >25%
- Use-case: small pilot with tight budget; 99.9% SLO achievable with autoscaling & KV caching

Option B — Staged Anchor (balanced):
- Cluster: 16x A100-80GB equiv (8 reserved, 8 burstable)
- Minimum floor: 8 GPUs reserved, 8 burstable with committed-to-burst credits
- Ramp: 4-week staged activation (2 GPUs -> 8 GPUs -> 16 GPUs), with an optional canary lane for major model versions
- Notes: Recommended for production-like pilot with embedding-heavy windows

Option C — Throughput-first (fast growth):
- Cluster: 32x A100-80GB equiv (mixed sizes)
- Minimum floor: 16 GPUs reserved, remaining on dedicated autoscale with warm pool
- Ramp: 6–8 week phased activation and capacity validation

Common recommendations:
- Min GPU footprint for acceptable latency under your profile: 8 GPUs (A100-80 equiv) with aggressive batching disabled for tail latency sensitive routes
- Warm-up credits: 2 weeks of free warm-up credits (token-based) + prefix cache pre-warm
- Fallback: automatic routing to a quantized 4-bit variant (lower-cost) for non-critical routes; fallback to dedicated-hosted shared pool for best-effort requests

Next steps: I can update the MSA addendum and pricing worksheet for procurement once you indicate which option. Can we schedule a 30-min procurement-ready walkthrough next Tue (10/12) or Thu (10/14)?

Attachment: LumenRx_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf (proposal draft)

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
